## Requirement matrix

Reviewed: 6 requirements, by level 4 MUST, 2 SHOULD; by status 6 satisfied, 0 unsupported, 0 not applicable.

Unreviewed: none. Every requirement the mechanical catalogue of RFC 868 holds has a status.

One row per requirement of [`overlay.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/rfcspec/blob/main/profiles/time/overlay.yaml), in its order. The source is the line span in RFC 868.

| Id | Level | Transports | Quote | Source | Status | Element or reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-TCP-1 | MUST | tcp | When the connection is established, the server returns a 32-bit time value | lines 44-45 | satisfied | tcp.server.D1-3-R-TCP-1-send-time |
| R-TCP-2 | MUST | tcp | the server returns a 32-bit time value and closes the connection. | lines 45-46 | satisfied | tcp.server.D1-6-R-TCP-2-close |
| R-TCP-3 | SHOULD | tcp | If the server is unable to determine the time at its site, it should either refuse the connection or close it without sending anything. | lines 46-48 | satisfied | tcp.server.R-TCP-3-unable-close |
| R-UDP-1 | MUST | udp | When a datagram arrives, the server returns a datagram containing the 32-bit time value. | lines 76-78 | satisfied | udp.server.D2-3-D2-4-R-UDP-1-reply-time |
| R-UDP-2 | SHOULD | udp | If the server is unable to determine the time at its site, it should discard the arriving datagram and make no reply. | lines 78-79 | satisfied | udp.server.R-UDP-2-discard |
| R-TIME-1 | MUST | tcp, udp | The time is the number of seconds since 00:00 (midnight) 1 January 1900 GMT | lines 83-84 | satisfied | layout.time |
